# The Problem


The CRAN packages for Likert-type data workflow, viz, @mollazehi2025; @winzar2026 and @bryer2025, did not encompass seamless _type coercion_ to alternative structures  for  robust downstream processing, but, facilitates standard Likert items workflows. They work with conventional, clean ordinal data formats and lack the native architectural framework required for structural transformations.

Empirical workflow frequently encounter non-standard data which require programmatic modification; such as mapping items/scales into ordinal factors, turning multi-point data into binary indicators, or synthesizing Likert scales from continuous data. The existing workflow cannot execute these natively, forcing researchers to rely on fragmented, manual workarounds and ad-hoc scripting. This fragmentation disrupts analysis, introduces data entry risks, and leads to loss of man-hours. This project proposes an open-source R package for automated type coercion and dynamic vector mapping to systematically bridge this gap while preserving data integrity, and handling non-standard data natively.
